skill.name: playwright-browser-automation
skill.description: Automate browser testing with Playwright by generating and running scripts for pages, forms, screenshots, responsive layouts, accessibility, and performance checks.
skill.summary: Generate and run Playwright browser automation for web testing tasks.
skill.author: DataFlight

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command hits are Markdown or JavaScript backtick false positives. Real risks remain because the skill runs Node and npm commands, executes generated Playwright scripts from /tmp, and saves screenshots to shared temporary paths. I found no evidence of prompt injection, hidden external callbacks, or obfuscated payloads in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Use a unique per-run directory with restricted permissions, random filenames, and cleanup before executing generated scripts.

remediation.issue: Local Node and npm commands are required
remediation.suggestion: Show the exact command and require explicit user confirmation before running setup or automation commands.

remediation.issue: Screenshots are saved in shared temporary paths
remediation.suggestion: Warn users when pages may contain sensitive data, and store outputs in a private run directory when possible.

remediation.issue: Browser automation can access user-provided URLs
remediation.suggestion: Prefer localhost or authorized test targets, and avoid production credentials unless the user explicitly approves.

content.value_statement: Manual browser checks are slow and inconsistent. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code create Playwright scripts for testing, screenshots, forms, and responsive layouts.
actual_capabilities: Detects local development servers before localhost testing.
Creates Playwright scripts for page, form, login, and responsive checks.
Runs Chromium automation through the plugin Node wrapper.
Captures screenshots for full pages, devices, and failure states.
Uses helpers for accessibility, performance, network, and data extraction tasks.
Supports inline automation for quick page checks.
limitations: Requires Playwright and Chromium setup before first use.
Runs local Node commands, so users should review commands before execution.
Needs a reachable URL or running local server for most tasks.
May capture sensitive page content in screenshots if used on private pages.

use_cases.title: Check Local Web Apps
use_cases.description: Find a running dev server, open the app, capture screenshots, and report page health issues.

use_cases.title: Validate Release Flows
use_cases.description: Exercise login, form submission, navigation, and link checks before a release.

use_cases.title: Review Responsive Behavior
use_cases.description: Test the same page across desktop, tablet, mobile, and named device viewports.

prompt_templates.title: Capture a Page Screenshot
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Playwright to open my local web app and capture a full page screenshot. Tell me which server you detected first.

prompt_templates.title: Test a Form Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Playwright to test the contact form at the URL I provide. Fill the visible fields, submit it, and report validation or success messages.

prompt_templates.title: Run Responsive Checks
prompt_templates.prompt: Test this page on desktop, tablet, and mobile viewports. Capture screenshots and list layout problems you observe.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Critical User Journey
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a Playwright script for the login and dashboard journey. Include console error capture, accessibility checks, and clear pass or fail notes.

output_examples.input: Check the local dashboard and take a screenshot.
output_examples.output: Detected one local server, opened the dashboard, saved a screenshot, and reported the page title and URL.

output_examples.input: Test the login flow on my staging URL.
output_examples.output: Filled the login form, submitted it, confirmed the dashboard redirect, and noted any console errors.

output_examples.input: Review this landing page on mobile and desktop.
output_examples.output: Captured screenshots for each viewport and summarized visible spacing, overflow, and navigation issues.

best_practices: Confirm the target URL and server before running automation.
Use test accounts and avoid production credentials during browser tests.
Review generated commands and output paths before execution.
anti_patterns: Do not run generated scripts against untrusted sites without review.
Do not store sensitive screenshots in shared temporary locations.
Do not assume localhost examples match every project port.

faq.question: Does this skill require Playwright?
faq.answer: Yes. The setup command installs Playwright and the Chromium browser before automation runs.

faq.question: Can it test a local development server?
faq.answer: Yes. It first checks for running local servers and can use the detected URL.

faq.question: Can it test external websites?
faq.answer: Yes, when you provide a URL and have permission to automate that site.

faq.question: Does it run commands on my computer?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses local Node commands to run Playwright scripts, so review commands before approval.

faq.question: Where are screenshots saved?
faq.answer: The examples save screenshots under temporary paths. Treat those files as sensitive if pages contain private data.

faq.question: Can it replace a full test suite?
faq.answer: No. It helps create and run focused browser checks, but teams should maintain versioned tests separately.
